title: Corpus consolidation — ledger index staleness gate
scope: Isolated ADR fixture trees plus a READ-ONLY run against the repository ledger. docs/adr/README.md was NOT regenerated by this pass.

implemented.check_index_mode: scripts/adr-index-gen.js gains --check-index: it regenerates the index table in memory and compares it byte-for-byte with README.md, failing with the first differing line and the exact regeneration command. --check-index implies --check, so record validation still runs first.
implemented.check_message: --check now states plainly that it neither writes nor compares the index, so its green result can no longer be read as an index guarantee.
implemented.ci_wiring: Wired into .github/workflows/invariants.yml as a `check-adr-index` step alongside the existing --check step. It is a separate flag rather than folded into --check so a record-validation failure and an index drift are distinguishable in the CI log.

repository_ledger_state.note: In sync at close (56 records), so the new CI step is green as landed. The index went briefly stale mid-pass while records were being added concurrently and --check-index detected that correctly before the owning change regenerated it. This pass did not regenerate the index itself.

  PASS the failure gives the regeneration command

16 passed, 0 failed
ok: 56 ADR(s) valid (--check, README neither written nor compared — use --check-index to compare)
ok: 56 ADR(s) valid and docs/adr/README.md is in sync

limitations: This gate compares the index with the records; it establishes nothing about semantic correctness, verified_paths accuracy, or whether a verified_commit reflects the current worktree. Legacy dispositions, governing-document routes and reader-route validation are untouched.
